agent_blueprint.title: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent
agent_blueprint.description: Finds anomalies in PoroTomo DAS records that could indicate injection-induced seismicity at Brady Hot Springs, runs the detection on Aurora through PBS, and estimates the probability of a Pohang-like (Mw >= 5.5) event with the Shapiro seismogenic-index model.

metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
Headline results — run directory /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (run ID run_20261115T155359Z_s20; summary.json generated 2026-11-15T16:02:33+00:00; original PBS job recorded in jobs.txt: 9092130.aurora-pbs-0001.hostmgmt.cm.aurora.alcf.anl.gov, 2 nodes x 24 ranks = 48 ranks, manifest of 759 records, started 2026-11-15T15:57:45Z). This session was READ-ONLY: no PBS job was submitted and hazard.py was not run; all values below were read directly from the run's files.

RECORDS ANALYSED
- 759 DAS records analysed, all with status "ok" (records.by_status {"ok": 759}, records.analysed = 759), stride 20, spanning 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (about 8 days), sampled_fraction_of_time = 0.033141355084075994 (~3.3% of total time), mean 2003.99 ms per record.

ANOMALOUS RECORDS AND DAS DETECTIONS
- Anomalous records: n_anomalous = 57 (z_threshold = 5.0; anomalies.csv has 57 data rows). Top anomaly: start 2016-03-23T20:50:17Z, zmax 30.92, driver max_sta_lta; max_sta_lta drives every top-10 record, with spectral_centroid_hz and n_events as secondary drivers.
- DAS detections: das_events.n = 62 (events.csv has 62 data rows), in 53 records; n_scaled_to_full_time = 1870.77; relative-magnitude Aki MLE b_relative = 0.9849352475487246, mc_relative = -0.8492463451632817, n_above_mc = 34.

SEISMOGENIC INDEX Sigma (exactly as summary.json gives it)
- b = 1.0: Sigma = -5.448901270028832
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.3193012700288325
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.280901270028833
- DAS upper bound: Sigma = -2.698279919032152

P(Mw >= 5.5) PER YEAR (at observed rate, exactly as summary.json gives it)
- b = 1.0: 0.00011982478978644906 (~1.20e-4 yr^-1)
- b = 0.73: 0.004921548824626587 (~4.92e-3 yr^-1)
- b = 0.65: 0.014735103451029574 (~1.47e-2 yr^-1)
- DAS-based upper bound (key literally named "das_upper_bound_OVERCOUNTS"): 0.07842182774171746 (~7.84e-2 yr^-1)
(Over the observed volume only: b=1.0 -> 5.235629034316958e-06; b=0.73 -> 0.00021553767643867072; b=0.65 -> 0.0006483793467004784; DAS upper bound -> 0.0024076054468051833.)

WHICH IS CALIBRATED AND WHICH IS AN UPPER BOUND
- The CALIBRATED probabilities are the catalog-based ones (hazard_catalog_based), anchored on the LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 local catalogue (catalog.source = "GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016": n = 5 events, Mc = -0.48, mag_max = 0.07, all ML magnitudes) with assumed b-values 1.0 / 0.73 / 0.65.
- The DAS-based number is an UPPER BOUND ONLY, not calibrated: it uses DAS relative magnitudes (b_source = "DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE", b_used = 0.9849352475487246) and over-counts because it treats every DAS detection as an event at/above the catalogue minimum magnitude (mc_relative = -0.849). Its magnitudes are relative/uncalibrated, so P(Mw>=5.5) = 0.0784 yr^-1 is a ceiling, not a calibrated estimate.

ASSUMPTIONS EACH NUMBER RESTS ON
- Catalog-based (calibrated): a very small local catalogue (only 5 LBNL/NCEDC events, Mc = -0.48, Mmax = 0.07, ML magnitudes); assumed Gutenberg-Richter b-values (1.0, 0.73, 0.65); extrapolation from that catalogue to Mw >= 5.5; and scaling the observed DAS-window rate (759 records, stride 20, only ~3.3% of the 16-day pumping window sampled) to a per-year rate.
- DAS upper bound: DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE b = 0.9849 with mc_relative = -0.849; every one of the 62 DAS detections counted as a real event at/above the catalogue minimum magnitude (hence the over-count), with uncalibrated (relative) magnitudes; same sampled-window-to-per-year scaling.
- Context from the same run: pumping window 2016-03-11T08:00Z to 2016-03-27T07:00Z (~15.96 days, source "GDR 917 corrected deployment data"), injected 465448.11 m3, extracted 505933.05 m3, net_injected -40484.94 m3 (extraction exceeded injection); hourly Spearman correlations of events vs net injection / |d net| / injection rate are all weakly negative (-0.1728, -0.0296, -0.0926), so the anomalies do not strongly track injection. For reference, the Sigma that would be needed for a 1% chance of Mw >= 5.5 over the observed volume is -2.1657 (b=1.0), -3.6507 (b=0.73), -4.0907 (b=0.65) — the site Sigma of -5.45 to -5.28 is far below all of these, so the catalog-based Pohang-like probabilities are small; only the uncalibrated DAS upper bound is large.
